requirement:
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.

For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
rationale: The three marked tests in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`. I read the implementation (`populate_in`) only to see what the index table renders. I did not use it to derive expected behavior. **Per-test fields, contributing runs and run separation** - `reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles` asserts index table rows containing attempt, capture time, run outcome / attempt outcome and the `contributes` state. - It also asserts `binary / one` and `binary / two` (binary and test name), `cargo nextest run` / `filtered` (command and selection), and the originating run id. - Its two runs have different revision and dirty values. It asserts `revision rev; dirty yes` for one run and `revision unknown; dirty unknown` for the other. Records from several runs are therefore shown per run rather than as one run. - `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` covers "including missing or stale coverage". It asserts `unavailable: incomplete` for a newest failed or interrupted attempt with no data. It asserts `stale: source inputs changed or unavailable` after the source changes. It asserts `historical build configuration` for an excluded configuration. **Union line coverage** - `file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files` has one location recorded in both the test process (positive count) and a child process (zero count). Another location appears only in the child, with `u64::MAX`. A third location has count zero, and a second file has a zero-count location. - The asserted total is `Line coverage: **2/4 (50.0%)**`. - That total confirms each location counts once in the denominator, that any positive count marks a location covered, and that child-process records are included. - In the reports test, one location is zero in the test process and positive in the child, and the asserted total is a fully covered `2/2 (100.0%)`. - In the filtered-runs test, two records each cover a different location. The asserted fully covered total confirms the union. An average across process reports would give 50%. - The half-covered assertion confirms a newer attempt with no coverage is not replaced by the older success. **Unavailable, incomplete and links** - The stale scenario in the filtered-runs test asserts `no fresh instrumented lines`. That text appears only in the branch that renders `Line coverage: **unavailable**`, so it covers "no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable". The assertion does not check the word "unavailable" itself, which is a minor weakness but not a gap. - The reports test asserts that the index contains `not establish that all current tests were measured`. This covers "MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage". - The `unavailable: incomplete` and stale assertions, plus the "Excluded coverage" counts checked in other tests, make incomplete coverage visible. - The reports test asserts that every detail chapter's href appears in the index and that each detail page links back. This covers the link to `requirements.test-coverage.index.details`. The remaining obligations are delegated to the cited `index.selection`, `index.freshness` and `index.details` requirements and to `rust_item_coverage`. Their own tests cover them. I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept. **Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed: the first determination was `true` and an independent second assessment's was `false`. A verifier checked the less favorable `false` determination and found none of its claimed gaps real, so `true` is recorded. Verification: **Claimed gap: no test asserts each selected test's capture time in the summary.** This is not real. - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#fn[populate_in]` builds the summary row as binary/test, attempt, `record.attempt.started`, outcomes, state, run, revision and dirty state, then command and selection. The "Captured (Unix ns)" column holds `attempt.started`, which is the capture time. - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[record]` sets `attempt.started` to its `start` argument. - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles]` calls `record(..., "one", 100, ...)` and `record(..., "two", 200, ...)`. It asserts that the index content contains `| 1 | 100 | success / success | contributes` and `| 1 | 200 | success / success | contributes`. In each row, the `1` is the attempt number and the next cell is the capture time (100 or 200). The assertion fixes the capture-time column's position and its distinct value for each test. - An implementation that dropped or blanked the capture time in the index would fail these assertions. The reviewer's counterexample is therefore ruled out. - The reviewer treated `Captured at Unix ns` on the detail chapters as the only capture-time assertion. That one belongs to `index.details`, but the index-row assertions above also cover the summary. **Other obligations.** I did not find a gap in these. - The tests assert the union line coverage `2/4` and `2/2`. - They assert `no fresh instrumented lines` for the unavailable case. - They assert `unavailable: incomplete`, stale, and historical-configuration states. - They assert the revision and dirty state, both known and unknown. - They assert the command and selection, the run id, the detail links, and the incompleteness disclaimer. **Weaker point (non-success outcomes in the outcome column).** The requirement says the index shows each test's outcome. `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` does not assert failed or interrupted text in the outcome column. It does assert the `unavailable: incomplete` state for those attempts. Outcome display is exercised by the `success / success` assertions. The column is a plain passthrough, so I do not count this as an established gap. No claimed gap is real, so nothing needs acknowledgment.

The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify

:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their retained per-process reports MUST remain
inspectable using their captured source until the build artifacts are removed.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
